title_en: Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Securities Companies

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Company Law") and the Securities Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Securities Law") for the purposes of strengthening the supervision and administration of securities companies, regulating the conduct of securities companies, preventing risks of securities companies, protecting the lawful rights and interests of clients and the public interest of society, and promoting the sound development of the securities industry.

Article 2 A securities company shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and the provisions of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, operate prudently, and perform its fiduciary duties to clients.

Article 3 Shareholders and actual controllers of a securities company shall not abuse their rights, misappropriate the assets of the securities company or its clients, or harm the lawful rights and interests of the securities company or its clients.

Article 4 The State encourages securities companies to carry out innovations in business modes, business or products, organization, and incentive and restraint mechanisms in accordance with law, on the premise of effectively controlling risks.
The securities regulatory authority under the State Council and relevant departments of the State Council shall take effective measures to promote the standardized and orderly conduct of innovation activities of securities companies.
Article 5 A securities company may issue, trade, and sell securities-type financial products in accordance with the provisions of the State.

Article 6 The securities regulatory authority under the State Council shall perform its supervision and administration duties over securities companies according to law. The dispatched offices of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council shall, within the scope of authorization by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, perform the supervision and administration duties over securities companies.

Article 7 The securities regulatory authority under the State Council, the People's Bank of China, and other financial regulatory authorities under the State Council shall establish an information sharing mechanism for the supervision and administration of securities companies.
The securities regulatory authority under the State Council and local people's governments shall establish a mechanism for the notification of relevant information on securities companies.

Article 8 The establishment of a securities company shall meet the conditions prescribed by the Company Law, the Securities Law, and these Regulations, and shall be subject to the approval of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 9 Shareholders of a securities company shall make capital contributions in currency or non-monetary property necessary for the operation of the securities company. The total amount of non-monetary property contributed by shareholders of a securities company shall not exceed 30% of the registered capital of the securities company.
The capital contributions of shareholders of a securities company shall be verified by an accounting firm with qualifications for securities and futures related businesses, which shall issue a certificate; the non-monetary property in the capital contributions shall be appraised by an asset appraisal institution with qualifications for securities related businesses.
Where, in the course of operation of a securities company, a creditor of the securities company converts its claims into equities of the securities company, such conversion shall not be subject to the restrictions set forth in the first paragraph of this Article.
Article 11 A securities company shall have at least three senior officers who have served as senior officers in the securities industry for a full term of two years.

Article 12 When a securities company is established, its business scope shall be commensurate with its financial condition, internal control system, compliance system, and human resources condition; during the operation of a securities company, upon its application, the securities regulatory authority under the State Council may adjust its business scope based on its financial condition, internal control level, degree of compliance, business management capability of senior officers, and number of professional personnel.

Article 14 Where any entity or individual falls under any of the following circumstances, it or he shall inform the securities company in advance, and the securities company shall report to the securities regulatory authority under the State Council for approval:
(1) After subscribing for or acquiring equities of a securities company, its or his shareholding ratio reaches 5% of the registered capital of the securities company;
(2) By holding equities of the shareholders of the securities company or by other means, it or he actually controls more than 5% of the equities of the securities company.
Without the approval of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, no entity or individual may entrust another person or accept entrustment from another person to hold or manage equities of a securities company. Shareholders of a securities company shall not, in violation of state provisions, agree to exercise voting rights not in proportion to their capital contributions.

Article 15 Where a securities company is merged or divided, any material transfer of assets involving the rights and interests of clients shall be appraised by an asset appraisal institution with qualifications for securities related businesses.
Where a securities company suspends business, dissolves, or becomes bankrupt, it shall obtain the approval of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, and shall arrange for clients and handle unfinished business in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 17 The company registration authority shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and based on the approval document issued by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, handle the registration of establishment, alteration, or cancellation of a securities company and its domestic branches.
After obtaining the business license for the securities company or its domestic branch issued or renewed by the company registration authority, the securities company shall apply to the securities regulatory authority under the State Council for the issuance or renewal of the securities business license. The securities business license shall specify the securities business scope of the securities company or its domestic branch.
Without obtaining the securities business license, a securities company and its domestic branches shall not engage in securities business.
Where a securities company ceases all securities business, dissolves, becomes bankrupt, or dissolves a domestic branch, it shall make a public announcement in the newspapers designated by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council and shall, in accordance with the provisions, surrender the securities business license to the securities regulatory authority under the State Council for cancellation.

Article 26 A securities company and its domestic branches that engage in the securities business as specified in Article 125 of the Securities Law shall comply with the provisions of the Securities Law and these Regulations.
A securities company and its domestic branches shall conduct business operations approved by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, and shall not conduct any business not approved.
Where two or more securities companies are controlled by the same entity or individual, or have a controlling relationship with each other, they shall not engage in the same securities business, unless otherwise provided by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 27 A securities company shall, in accordance with the principle of prudent operation, establish and improve risk management and internal control systems to prevent and control risks.
A securities company shall implement centralized and unified management of its branches, and shall not jointly operate or co-manage branches with others, nor contract out, lease, or entrust the operation and management of branches to others.

Article 28 Where a securities company, entrusted by a securities registration and clearing institution, opens securities accounts for clients, it shall verify the authenticity of the name or title and identity declared by the client in accordance with the rules on securities account management. The name or title of the fund account and the securities account opened for the same client shall be consistent.
Where a securities company opens securities accounts for securities asset management clients, it shall report them to the stock exchange for record within three trading days from the date of account opening.
A securities company shall not provide the client's fund account or securities account to others for use.

Article 29 A securities company engaging in securities asset management business, margin trading business, or selling securities-type financial products shall, in accordance with prescribed procedures, understand the client's identity, property and income status, securities investment experience and risk preference, and record and retain such information in written and electronic form. The securities company shall recommend appropriate products or services based on the understood client situation. The specific rules shall be formulated by the Securities Association of China.

Article 30 Before concluding contracts for securities trading orders, securities asset management, margin trading and other business with a client, a securities company shall designate a special person in advance to explain the relevant business rules and contract contents to the client, and have the risk disclosure statement signed by the client for confirmation. The mandatory clauses of business contracts and the standard form of risk disclosure statements shall be formulated by the Securities Association of China and reported to the securities regulatory authority under the State Council for record.

Article 31 A securities company engaging in securities asset management business or margin trading business shall prepare account statements in accordance with regulations and send them to clients on a monthly basis. If otherwise agreed with the client on the time or method of delivering account statements, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 32 A securities company shall establish an information inquiry system to ensure that clients can, at any time during the business hours of the securities company, inquire about their order records, transaction records, securities and fund balances, as well as the names, practice certificate numbers and securities broker certificate numbers of the securities company's business handling personnel and securities brokers.
Where a client believes that the relevant information records do not match the actual circumstances, the client may lodge a complaint with the securities company or the securities regulatory authority under the State Council. The securities company shall designate a specific department to handle client complaints. The securities regulatory authority under the State Council shall take corresponding measures based on the client's complaint.
Article 33 A securities company shall not, in violation of regulations, entrust other entities or individuals to carry out client solicitation, client service, or product sales activities.

Article 34 When providing investment advice to clients, a securities company shall not make definitive judgments on the rise or fall of securities prices or the market trend.
A securities company and its employees shall not use the provision of investment advice to clients to seek illegitimate benefits.

Article 35 A securities company shall establish and implement effective management systems to prevent its employees from holding or trading stocks directly or under aliases or in others' names, or from accepting stocks given by others.
Article 36 A securities company shall set aside general risk reserves in accordance with regulations to cover operating losses.

Article 37 A securities company engaging in securities brokerage business shall verify whether the funds and securities in the client's account are sufficient. If the funds in the client's fund account are insufficient, the securities company shall not accept the client's buy order; if the securities in the client's securities account are insufficient, the securities company shall not accept the client's sell order.

Article 38 A securities company engaging in securities brokerage business may entrust persons other than the securities company's employees as securities brokers to act on its behalf in carrying out client solicitation, client service and other activities. Securities brokers shall have securities practice qualifications.
A securities company shall conclude an agency contract with the entrusted securities broker, issue a securities broker certificate, specify the scope of authorization for the securities broker, and supervise the securities broker's practice.
Securities brokers shall conduct business within the scope authorized by the securities company and shall present the securities broker certificate to clients.

Article 39 Securities brokers shall comply with the management regulations applicable to employees of securities companies. Acts within the scope authorized by the securities company shall be subject to the corresponding legal liability of the securities company in accordance with law; acts beyond the scope of authorization shall be subject to the corresponding legal liability of the securities broker in accordance with law.
A securities broker may only accept entrustment from one securities company to carry out client solicitation, client service and other activities.
A securities broker shall not handle matters such as securities subscription or trading for clients.

Article 40 The fees charged by a securities company to clients for securities transactions shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State, and the items and standards of fees shall be publicized in a conspicuous place at the business premises.

Article 41 A securities company engaging in proprietary securities trading shall be limited to buying and selling stocks, bonds, warrants, securities investment funds that are publicly issued according to law, or other securities recognized by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 42 A securities company engaging in proprietary securities trading shall use real-name proprietary securities accounts.
The proprietary securities accounts of a securities company shall be reported to the stock exchange for record within three trading days from the date of account opening.

Article 44 When a securities company engages in proprietary securities trading, risk control indicators such as the ratio of the total value of proprietary securities to the company's net capital, the ratio of the value of holding one type of security to the company's net capital, and the ratio of the quantity of holding one type of security to the total issuance of that security shall comply with the provisions of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 45 A securities company may, in accordance with the provisions of the Securities Law and these Regulations, engage in securities asset management business by accepting clients' entrustment and using clients' assets for investment. The gains arising from the investment shall be enjoyed by the client, and the losses shall be borne by the client. The securities company may charge management fees in accordance with the agreement.
Where a securities company engages in securities asset management business, it shall conclude a securities asset management contract with the client, stipulating matters such as the investment scope, investment proportion, management period and management fees.

Article 47. Where a securities company uses the assets of multiple clients to conduct collective investment, it shall comply with the relevant provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 48. For the purpose of these Regulations, margin trading business refers to the business activities in which, in securities transactions conducted on a stock exchange or other securities trading venues approved by the State Council, a securities company lends funds to a client for the purchase of securities or lends securities to a client for sale, and the client deposits corresponding collateral.

Article 50. A securities company engaging in margin trading business shall enter into a margin trading contract with the client, and, in accordance with the provisions of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council, open a client securities collateral account in the name of the securities company with the securities registration and settlement institution, and open a client funds collateral account with a designated commercial bank. The funds in the client funds collateral account shall be managed by reference to the provisions of Article 57 of these Regulations.
Within the client securities collateral account and the client funds collateral account opened in the name of the securities company, a credit account shall be separately opened for each client.

Article 51. When a securities company provides margin financing to a client, it shall use its own funds or funds raised according to law; when it provides securities lending to a client, it shall use its own securities or securities over which it has obtained the right of disposal according to law.

Article 52. When a securities company provides margin trading to a client, the client shall deposit a certain proportion of margin. The margin may be satisfied by securities.
The margin deposited by the client and all securities purchased and all funds obtained from the sale of securities through margin trading transactions shall be collateral for the securities company, and shall be deposited into the securities company's client securities collateral account or client funds collateral account and recorded in the client's credit account.

Article 53. The securities in the client securities collateral account and the funds in the client funds collateral account shall be trust property. A securities company shall not violate its fiduciary duty to misappropriate the securities or funds in the client's collateral accounts. Except for the circumstances provided for in Article 54 of these Regulations or other circumstances otherwise agreed upon according to law between the securities company and the client, the securities company shall not use the securities or funds in the client's collateral accounts.

Article 54. A securities company shall calculate on a daily basis the ratio of the value of the client's collateral to its debt. When such ratio falls below the prescribed minimum maintenance margin ratio, the securities company shall notify the client to make up the difference within a specified period. If the client fails to make up the difference within the specified period, or fails to repay the margin trading debt at maturity, the securities company shall immediately dispose of its collateral in accordance with the agreement.

Article 55. The proportion of margin to be deposited by a client in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 52 of these Regulations shall be prescribed by the unit authorized by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.
The types of securities that a securities company may lend to clients, the types of securities that the funds lent may be used to purchase, the types and conversion rates of marketable securities that may be used as margin, the term of margin trading, the minimum maintenance margin ratio, and the period for making up the difference shall be prescribed by the stock exchange.
The relevant provisions made by the authorized unit or the stock exchange as specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall be filed with the securities regulatory authority under the State Council and shall not violate national monetary policy.

Article 56. Where a securities company engaging in margin trading business has insufficient own funds or securities, it may borrow from a securities finance company. The establishment and dissolution of securities finance companies shall be determined by the State Council.

Article 18 A securities company shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law, the Securities Law, and these Regulations, establish a sound organizational structure and define the functions of the decision-making, execution, and supervision bodies.

Article 19 A securities company may have independent directors. Independent directors of a securities company shall not hold any position outside the board of directors in the securities company, and shall not have any relationship with the securities company that may interfere with their independent and objective judgment.

Article 20 Where a securities company operates two or more of the following: securities brokerage business, securities asset management business, margin trading business, and securities underwriting and sponsorship business, its board of directors shall establish a compensation and nomination committee, an audit committee, and a risk control committee, which shall exercise the functions prescribed in the articles of association of the securities company.
Where a securities company establishes a compensation and nomination committee and an audit committee in its board of directors, the heads of such committees shall be independent directors.

Article 21 A securities company shall have a secretary to the board of directors, who shall be responsible for preparing the shareholders' meeting and board of directors meetings, keeping documents, and managing shareholder information, and shall provide relevant information according to law and handle matters of information submission or information disclosure in accordance with the regulations or as required by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council, shareholders, or other relevant entities or individuals. The secretary to the board of directors shall be a senior officer of the securities company.

Article 22 Where a securities company establishes an institution that exercises the operational and management authority of the securities company, it shall specify in the company's articles of association the name, composition, duties, and rules of procedure of such institution, and the members of such institution shall be senior officers of the securities company.

Article 23 A securities company shall have a compliance officer, who shall review, supervise, or inspect the legality and compliance of the securities company's operational and management activities. The compliance officer shall be a senior officer of the securities company, shall be appointed by the board of directors, and shall be subject to approval by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council. The compliance officer shall not concurrently hold a position responsible for operational management in the securities company.
If the compliance officer discovers any illegal or non-compliant act, they shall report it to the institution specified in the company's articles of association, and at the same time report it to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council or the relevant self-regulatory organization in accordance with the regulations.
If a securities company dismisses its compliance officer, it shall have justifiable reasons, and shall report in writing the facts and reasons for the dismissal to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council within three working days from the date of dismissal.

Article 24 Directors, supervisors, and senior officers of a securities company shall, prior to taking office, obtain the qualifications for the position approved by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council.
A securities company shall not appoint or elect any person who has not obtained the qualifications for the position to hold the office specified in the preceding paragraph; if such appointment or election has already been made, the resolution or decision on the appointment or election shall be null and void.

Article 25 If the legal representative or a senior officer of a securities company leaves office, the securities company shall conduct an audit on such person, and shall submit the audit report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council within two months from the date of the person's departure. If the legal representative or the principal person responsible for operational management of a securities company leaves office, an accounting firm with qualifications for securities and futures related businesses shall be engaged to conduct an audit on such person.
If the audit report specified in the preceding paragraph is not submitted to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council, the departing person shall not hold any position in another securities company.
Business rules and risk control

Article 57 Where a securities company engages in securities brokerage business, the trading settlement funds of its clients shall be deposited with a designated commercial bank, and shall be managed in separate accounts opened in the name of each client.
The designated commercial bank shall enter into a client trading settlement fund depository contract with the securities company and its clients, stipulating matters such as the deposit, withdrawal, transfer, and inquiry of the client's trading settlement funds, and shall open a master account for the client's trading settlement funds for the securities company in accordance with the requirements of net settlement of securities transactions and delivery against payment.
The deposit and withdrawal of a client's trading settlement funds shall be handled through the designated commercial bank. The designated commercial bank shall ensure that the client can inquire about the balance and changes of the client's trading settlement funds at any time.
The list of designated commercial banks shall be determined and announced by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 58 Where a securities company engages in securities asset management business, it shall entrust the client's entrusted assets to the designated commercial bank specified in Article 57(4) of these Regulations or to another asset custodian institution recognized by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council for custody.
The asset custodian institution shall, in accordance with the provisions of the securities regulatory authority of the State Council and the terms of the securities asset management contract, perform the duties of safely keeping the client's entrusted assets, handling fund receipt and payment matters, and supervising the securities company's investment activities.

Article 59 The trading settlement funds of a client and the entrusted assets of a securities asset management client shall belong to the client, and shall be independent from and managed separately from the proprietary assets of the securities company, the designated commercial bank, and the asset custodian institution. Unless due to the client's own debts or other circumstances provided by law, no entity or individual may apply for seizure, freezing, or compulsory execution of the client's trading settlement funds or entrusted assets.

Article 61 A securities company shall not provide financing or guarantee to others using the assets of its securities brokerage clients or securities asset management clients. No entity or individual may compel, instruct, assist, or accept a securities company to provide financing or guarantee using the assets of its securities brokerage clients or securities asset management clients.

Article 62 A designated commercial bank, an asset custodian institution, and a securities depository and clearing institution shall supervise the use of the trading settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in clients' collateral accounts deposited with it, and shall periodically submit to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council the relevant data on the depository or use of the clients' trading settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in clients' collateral accounts in accordance with the regulations.
A designated commercial bank, an asset custodian institution, and a securities depository and clearing institution shall reject any application or instruction to use the clients' trading settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in clients' collateral accounts beyond the scope specified in Articles 53, 54, and 60 of these Regulations. If they discover that the clients' trading settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in clients' collateral accounts have been illegally used or are otherwise abnormal, they shall immediately report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council, and send a copy to the relevant regulatory authority.

Article 63 A securities company shall submit an annual report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council within four months from the end of each fiscal year, and shall submit a monthly report within seven working days from the end of each month.
If a major event occurs that affects or may affect the securities company's operational management, financial condition, risk control indicators, or the safety of client assets, the securities company shall immediately submit an interim report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council, explaining the cause of the event, its current status, the potential consequences, and the corresponding measures to be taken.

Article 64 The financial accounting report, the risk control indicator report, and other special reports as prescribed by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council in the annual report of a securities company shall be audited by an accounting firm with qualifications for securities and futures related businesses. The annual report of a securities company shall be accompanied by an internal control assessment report issued by such accounting firm.
The directors and senior officers of a securities company shall sign and confirm the annual report; the principal person responsible for operational management and the person in charge of finance shall sign and confirm the monthly report. The persons who sign the annual report or monthly report of the securities company shall ensure that the contents of the report are truthful, accurate, and complete; if they hold dissenting opinions on the contents of the report, they shall note their opinions and reasons.

Article 65 The securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall designate persons to review the annual reports and monthly reports submitted by securities companies, and shall prepare review reports. The reviewers shall sign the review reports. If problems are found during the review, the securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall promptly take appropriate measures.
The securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall compare and verify the relevant data submitted by the relevant institutions on clients' trading settlement funds, entrusted funds, and funds and securities in clients' collateral accounts, so as to timely discover any illegal use of funds or securities.

Article 66 A securities company shall publicly disclose its basic information, shareholding and controlling interests, liabilities and contingent liabilities, operational management status, financial revenue and expenditure, remuneration of senior officers, and other relevant information according to law. The specific measures shall be formulated by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 69 The materials and information disclosed, submitted, or provided by a securities company and the relevant entities and individuals shall be truthful, accurate, and complete, and shall not contain any false records, misleading statements, or material omissions.

Article 71 If any entity or individual, without approval, holds or actually controls 5% or more of the equity of a securities company, the securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall order it to make corrections within a specified period; before the correction, the corresponding equity shall not have voting rights.

Article 72 If any person who has not obtained the qualification for a position actually exercises the powers of a director, supervisor, senior officer, or person-in-charge of a domestic branch of a securities company, the securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall order him to cease exercising such powers, make a public announcement, and may take measures to ban him from the securities market in accordance with the provisions.

Article 73 If a director, supervisor, senior officer, or person-in-charge of a domestic branch of a securities company no longer meets the conditions for the qualification for a position, the securities company shall remove him from his post and report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council; if the securities company fails to remove him, the securities regulatory authority of the State Council shall order the removal.

Article 74 If a securities company engages or dismisses an accounting firm, it shall, within three working days from the date of making the decision, report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council for the record; if it dismisses an accounting firm, it shall state the reasons.

Article 75 When an accounting firm audits a securities company or its relevant personnel, it may consult and copy client information related to the audit matters or other relevant documents and materials of the securities company, and may retrieve relevant data and materials from the computer information management system of the securities company.
The accounting firm shall keep confidential the information obtained. Unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 76 A stock exchange shall conduct real-time monitoring of the trading activities of the proprietary securities accounts and securities asset management accounts of securities companies; if it discovers any abnormal circumstances, it shall promptly handle them in accordance with the trading rules and membership management rules, and report to the securities regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 78 If a securities company, when engaging in securities brokerage business, accepts a buy order from a client whose funds are insufficient, or accepts a sell order from a client whose securities are insufficient, it shall be punished in accordance with Article 205 of the Securities Law.
Article 79 If a securities company provides a client's fund account or securities account for use by another person, it shall be punished in accordance with Article 208 of the Securities Law.

Article 80 If a securities company induces a client to engage in unnecessary securities transactions, or when engaging in securities asset management business, uses client assets to conduct unnecessary securities transactions, it shall be punished in accordance with Article 210 of the Securities Law.

Article 81 If a securities company or its domestic branch engages in business beyond the scope approved by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council, it shall be punished in accordance with Article 219 of the Securities Law.

Article 82 If a securities company conducts transactions between its proprietary securities account and securities asset management accounts, or between different securities asset management accounts, and there is no sufficient evidence to prove that effective segregation has been achieved according to law, it shall be punished in accordance with Article 220 of the Securities Law.

Article 85 If a securities company fails to open an account for a client in accordance with provisions, it shall be ordered to make corrections; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed, and the directly responsible directors, senior officers, and other directly liable persons shall be imposed a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan.
Article 90 If a securities company collects fees in violation of regulations, the relevant competent authority shall impose punishment according to law.

Article 91 If a securities company's operation of securities business does not comply with the provisions of Paragraph 3 of Article 26 of these Regulations, it shall meet the prescribed requirements within the time limit specified by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 92 Where the depository method for transaction settlement funds of a securities company's customers does not conform to the provisions of Article 57 of these Regulations, the securities regulatory authority under the State Council shall order it to make adjustments within a specified time limit.
The depository method for transaction settlement funds of a securities company's customers shall meet the prescribed requirements within one year from the date on which these Regulations come into force.

Article 93 A securities company may borrow debts with repayment priority subordinated to ordinary debts from its shareholders or other entities. The specific administrative measures shall be formulated by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council.

Article 94 The business scope of a foreign-invested securities company, the qualification conditions and capital contribution ratio of its overseas shareholders shall be prescribed by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council and shall be submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 95 An overseas securities business institution that intends to engage in securities business within the territory of China or to establish a representative office shall obtain the approval of the securities regulatory authority under the State Council. The specific measures shall be formulated by the securities regulatory authority under the State Council and shall be submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 96 For the purposes of these Regulations, a securities registration and clearing institution refers to the securities registration and clearing institution as prescribed in Article 155 of the Securities Law.
Article 97 These Regulations shall come into force as of June 1, 2008.
